biography: Luke Hines, a name whispered with a mix of admiration and exasperation in British racing circles, hails from a small village in Oxfordshire. His journey began not in a karting track, but behind the wheel of his grandfather's battered Land Rover on muddy farmland. He learned car control sliding through fields, a skill that would later translate surprisingly well to the track. His first foray into competitive racing came at the late age of 19, entering a local Ginetta series on a shoestring budget. Early promise was evident, flashes of brilliance interspersed with rookie errors and the occasional spectacular crash. After several seasons honing his craft, Hines finally achieved a breakthrough in 2021, winning the Ginetta GT4 Supercup. This earned him a factory-backed drive, but the pressure seemed to amplify his inherent inconsistency. He's currently competing in the British GT Championship, still chasing that elusive overall championship title, and battling the demons of his own unpredictable nature.
drivingStyle: Hines is known for his aggressive, bordering on reckless, driving style. He's a late-braking specialist, often diving down the inside of corners where others wouldn't dare. While this boldness sometimes pays off with stunning overtakes, it also leads to avoidable collisions and costly mistakes. Tire management is a known weakness, as he tends to overdrive the car early in a stint, leaving him vulnerable in the closing laps. Under pressure, Hines can either perform miracles or completely unravel, making him a thrilling but unpredictable competitor.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from their Ginetta Junior days. Thornton is the methodical, consistent driver, the antithesis of Hines, and they've clashed on track numerous times.
A more recent rivalry fueled by an on-track incident at Brands Hatch where Hines punted Rossi off the track while battling for the lead, sparking accusations of deliberate foul play.
Hines and Bell are constantly neck and neck, with an uncanny ability to match each other's pace. Their races are typically a close battle of skill, with either driver able to come out on top.

quirks: Always wears a lucky pair of socks, despite having a sponsor-provided racing suit
Listens to heavy metal music at an extremely high volume right up until the moment he gets into the car.
Has a pre-race ritual of drawing a small, childlike picture of a race car on his steering wheel with a dry-erase marker.
famousQuote: "You can't win if you don't risk it. Sometimes that means going for a gap that's barely there. Sometimes it means ending up in the gravel. But you gotta send it."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2021 Ginetta GT4 Supercup championship after a nail-biting final race at Donington Park, securing victory with a last-lap overtake.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final race of the 2022 British GT Championship at Silverstone, costing his team the championship title.
